greet.speaker: Pisces
greet.text: A [Necromancer], yes — and before your hand drifts to that sword, no, nothing in this square has been raised. I merely occupy the cheapest air the Guild permits. Pisces Jealnv. You reek of a body that has never once held mana. Curious. You want something.

text_variants.text: The pupil returns. Your channels are... adequate now. Do try not to embarrass the discipline in public.
Back again. Either you are braver than the Watch or you have reconsidered your ignorance. Which is it?

options.text: You're a mage. Teach me to cast.

options._comment: Social Pillar II Phase B: stage-2 hub topic, lifted verbatim from docs/design/social-2-staging/pisces_stages.json (staging_note/_flag stripped). CANON tread-light: father a [Fencer] is staged (mild); the sold-rapier line is an OBLIQUE Wistram-era nod. HARD RAILS (absolute, per the companion doc): no expulsion cause, no deaths, no Az'kerash, no Ceria specifics. Appended AFTER 'Never mind.' (array end) so it can never shift an earlier option's visible index.
options.text: You hold yourself like a swordsman, not a scholar.

options._comment: Magical Door plan Task D3 (issue #8 spec §1 beat 2, the 3-path mage-consult opener). Requires door_chain_started (Erin's flicker beat, erin_errand.json), hide_when door_understood (the shared convergence counter -- 3-path identity rule) so it stops offering once ANY leg resolves. Appended at array END (index-safety convention, matches pisces_fence above).
options.text: Something's come through our pantry door. Will you look at it?

options._comment: Magical Door plan Task D3: the SKILL leg's REPORT step (cisterns_scout/wrong_order precedent -- [Observe]-ing pantry_door_runes in the inn alone only banks the intermediate read_the_door_runes; reporting the finding here banks the shared door_understood + pedestal_unsealed). The player's own line restates Pisces's TALK-leg verdict verbatim (consult_talk_done below) -- deliberate identity-rule parity, both legs arrive at the SAME understanding.
options.text: I read the wardwork myself: a spatial anchor, something that remembers being elsewhere.

door_consult.speaker: Pisces
door_consult.text: A door with opinions. How very like this city. Three ways to satisfy my curiosity: bleed for it, talk me into caring, or prove you can read a ward without my help. Choose, and don't waste my morning.

options.text: I'll clear whatever's coming through myself.
Come look at it yourself. Your kind of magic, not mine.
I'll read the wardwork myself, then.

consult_fight_response.speaker: Pisces
consult_fight_response.text: Bleeding it is. Predictable, but effective. Go on, then. I'll be here, dry and uninjured, exactly as planned.

consult_talk_pitch.speaker: Pisces
consult_talk_pitch.text: You want me to walk into someone's pantry and grope at a wild ward with my bare senses. No. I have wards of my own I'd rather keep.

options.text: It's not asking much. You'd know in a glance.

consult_talk_argue.speaker: Pisces
consult_talk_argue.text: ...A glance. Hm. If it truly reads as spatial and not necrotic, I could examine it without touching a thing. Fine, for the intellectual insult of not knowing, not for you.

consult_talk_done._comment: Magical Door plan Task D3 (issue #8 spec §3 Pisces TALK key, quoted verbatim).
consult_talk_done.speaker: Pisces
consult_talk_done.text: A spatial anchor. Crude. Fascinating. Whoever built your inn, adventurer, built it on something that remembers being elsewhere.

consult_skill_response.speaker: Pisces
consult_skill_response.text: Read it yourself, then. [Observe] the frame close, and mind that the pattern doesn't repeat the same way twice. Report back if you actually understand what you saw. I'll judge whether you do.

consult_skill_report.speaker: Pisces
consult_skill_report.text: ...Correct. Aggravatingly correct. You have the eye, if not the training. Don't let it go to your head. The training is where the real work is.

pisces_fence.speaker: Pisces
pisces_fence.text: ...Observant. A rapier, in fact, before any of this. My father's trade — his grip, his footwork, his opinions on both. I set it down for magic, and he has yet to forgive either of us. The footwork stayed. It wins me arguments the diction loses.

pisces_fence_two.speaker: Pisces
pisces_fence_two.text: I sold the blade years ago, when circumstances were... instructive. One does not miss a thing so much as the hands remember it. A sniff. Next question — preferably about magic, which unlike the past improves under examination.

lesson_mana.speaker: Pisces
lesson_mana.text: Then attend. Every living thing carries a reserve — mana. You will feel it as a second breath: a well that empties as you work a spell and refills when you sleep. A warrior spends stamina; you now spend this. Waste it and you are left waving your hands at the air.

options.text: How is casting different from swinging a blade?

lesson_casting.speaker: Pisces
lesson_casting.text: A sword asks only your arm. A spell asks your mind and your mana in the same instant: intent, shape, and cost, released together or not at all. Fumble any one of the three and you have merely gestured. Precision, traveler. Whatever the Watch mutters about my craft, it taught me precision.

options.text: So what do I cast first?

lesson_light.speaker: Pisces
lesson_light.text: [Light]. Always [Light]. It is cheap, it is obedient, and it fails without a corpse, a fire, or an inquest. Kindle one steady orb and you have proven the channel holds. Master that, and only then do we discuss the interesting spells.

options.text: I'm ready. Show me the words.

sealed.speaker: Pisces
sealed.text: There. The channel is opened — crudely, but opened. Sleep on it; the shape settles by morning, as these things do. And, traveler, when your first orb kindles, you will understand why I do not apologize for what I am.
